sanskrit: kāraṇaṃ bhāvitaṃ tasya sarvamuktasya sarvataḥ etad deveṣu duṣprāpaṃ manuṣyeṣu na labhyate
english: The cause of such devotion has been ordained for him who is wholly liberated in every way; this is hard to attain even among the gods, and is not to be had among men.

sanskrit: nirvighnā niścalā rudre bhaktir avyabhicāriṇī tasyaiva ca prasādena bhaktir utpadyate nṛṇām yayā yānti parāṃ siddhiṃ tadbhāvagatacetasaḥ
english: Unobstructed, unwavering, and unswerving is devotion to Rudra; and it is by his grace alone that such devotion arises in men, by which those whose minds are fixed upon his being attain the supreme perfection.

sanskrit: ye sarvabhāvopagatāḥ paratvenābhavan narāḥ prapannavatsalo devaḥ saṃsārāt tān samuddharet
english: Those men who have come to him with their whole being, taking him as the Supreme, the god who cherishes those who take refuge in him would lift up out of the round of existence.

sanskrit: evam anye na kurvanti devāḥ saṃsāramocanam manuṣyāṇāṃ mahādevād anyatrāpi tapobalāt
english: Thus the other gods do not accomplish the release of men from the cycle of birth, not even by the power of austerity, as does Mahādeva.

sanskrit: iti tenendrakalpena bhagavān sadasatpatiḥ kṛttivāsāḥ stutaḥ kṛṣṇa taṇḍinā śuddhabuddhinā
english: Thus, O Kṛṣṇa, was the Blessed One, lord of the existent and the nonexistent, clad in his hide, praised by Taṇḍi—one like unto Indra and of purified understanding.

sanskrit: stavam etaṃ bhagavato brahmā svayam adhārayat brahmā provāca śakrāya śakraḥ provāca mṛtyave
english: This hymn to the Blessed One Brahmā himself bore in memory; Brahmā declared it to Śakra, and Śakra declared it to Death.

sanskrit: mṛtyuḥ provāca rudrāṇāṃ rudrebhyas taṇḍim āgamat mahatā tapasā prāptas taṇḍinā brahmasadmani
english: Death declared it to the Rudras, and from the Rudras it came to Taṇḍi; by mighty austerity it was won by Taṇḍi in the abode of Brahmā.

sanskrit: taṇḍiḥ provāca śukrāya gautamāyāha bhārgavaḥ vaivasvatāya manave gautamaḥ prāha mādhava
english: Taṇḍi declared it to Śukra; the descendant of Bhṛgu spoke it to Gautama; and Gautama spoke it, O Mādhava, to Manu the son of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇāya sādhyāya manur iṣṭāya dhīmate yamāya prāha bhagavān sādhyo nārāyaṇo 'cyutaḥ
english: Manu spoke it to Nārāyaṇa the Sādhya, his beloved and wise one; and the blessed Sādhya, the imperishable Nārāyaṇa, spoke it to Yama.

sanskrit: nāciketāya bhagavān āha vaivasvato yamaḥ mārkaṇḍeyāya vārṣṇeya nāciketo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: The blessed Yama, son of Vivasvat, spoke it to Nāciketas; and Nāciketas, O scion of the Vṛṣṇis, spoke it to Mārkaṇḍeya.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeyān mayā prāptaṃ niyamena janārdana tavāpy aham amitraghna stavaṃ dadmy adya viśrutam svargyam ārogyam āyuṣyaṃ dhanyaṃ balyaṃ tathaiva ca
english: From Mārkaṇḍeya I received it through self-discipline, O Janārdana; and to you too, O slayer of foes, I now give this renowned hymn—conferring heaven, health, long life, prosperity, and strength as well.

sanskrit: na tasya vighnaṃ kurvanti dānavā yakṣarākṣasāḥ piśācā yātudhānāś ca guhyakā bhujagā api
english: No hindrance do the Dānavas work upon him, nor the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the Piśācas and the demons that devour, the Guhyakas, nor even the serpents.

sanskrit: yaḥ paṭheta śucir bhūtvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ abhagnayogo varṣaṃ tu so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: He who, having become pure, chaste, and master of his senses, recites it for a year with unbroken discipline obtains the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca mahāyogī tataḥ prāha kṛṣṇadvaipāyano muniḥ paṭhasva putra bhadraṃ te prīyatāṃ te maheśvaraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the great yogin, the sage Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, spoke: "Recite it, my son—blessings upon you; may Maheśvara be pleased with you.

sanskrit: purā putra mayā merau tapyatā paramaṃ tapaḥ putrahetor mahārāja stava eṣo 'nukīrtitaḥ
english: Of old, my son, while I performed the highest austerity upon Meru for the sake of offspring, O great king, this hymn was recited by me.

sanskrit: labdhavān asmi tān kāmān ahaṃ vai pāṇḍunandana tathā tvam api śarvād dhi sarvān kāmān avāpsyasi
english: I obtained those desires of mine, O delight of Pāṇḍu's line; and you too shall obtain all your desires from Śarva."

sanskrit: catuḥśīrṣas tataḥ prāha śakrasya dayitaḥ sakhā ālambāyana ity eva viśrutaḥ karuṇātmakaḥ
english: Then the Four-headed one spoke, the beloved friend of Śakra, renowned by the name Ālambāyana, whose nature was compassion:

sanskrit: mayā gokarṇam āsādya tapas taptvā śataṃ samāḥ ayonijānāṃ dāntānāṃ dharmajñānāṃ suvarcasām
english: "Having reached Gokarṇa and performed austerity there for a hundred years, I won—of sons not born of any womb, self-controlled, knowers of dharma, and radiant,

sanskrit: ajarāṇām aduḥkhānāṃ śatavarṣasahasriṇām labdhaṃ putraśataṃ śarvāt purā pāṇḍunṛpātmaja
english: of the ageless, the sorrowless, who live a hundred thousand years—a hundred sons from Śarva of old, O son of King Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: vālmīkiś cāpi bhagavān yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata vivāde sāmni munibhir brahmaghno vai bhavān iti uktaḥ kṣaṇena cāviṣṭas tenādharmeṇa bhārata
english: The blessed Vālmīki too addressed Yudhiṣṭhira: "In a dispute over a Sāman chant I was told by the sages, 'You are a slayer of a brāhmaṇa,' and in an instant, O Bhārata, I was possessed by that unrighteousness.

sanskrit: so 'ham īśānam anagham astauṣaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ muktaś cāsmy avaśaḥ pāpāt tato duḥkhavināśanaḥ āha māṃ tripuraghno vai yaśas te 'gryaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: Then I, taking refuge, praised the sinless Lord Īśāna, and helpless though I was, I was freed from that sin; and he, the destroyer of suffering, the slayer of Tripura, said to me, 'Your glory shall be foremost.'"

sanskrit: jāmadagnyaś ca kaunteyam āha dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ ṛṣimadhye sthitas tāta tapann iva vibhāvasuḥ
english: And the son of Jamadagni, foremost of the upholders of dharma, addressed the son of Kuntī, standing amid the seers like blazing fire, dear child:

sanskrit: pitṛvipravadhenāham ārto vai pāṇḍavāgraja śucir bhūtvā mahādevaṃ gatavāñ śaraṇaṃ nṛpa
english: "Tormented by the slaying of my father and of brāhmaṇas, O eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, having made myself pure, I went for refuge to Mahādeva, O king.

sanskrit: nāmabhiś cāstuvaṃ devaṃ tatas tuṣṭo 'bhavad bhavaḥ paraśuṃ ca dadau devo divyāny astrāṇi caiva me
english: With his names I praised the god, and thereupon Bhava was pleased; and the god gave me the axe and divine weapons as well.

sanskrit: pāpaṃ na bhavitā te 'dya ajeyaś ca bhaviṣyasi na te prabhavitā mṛtyur yaśasvī ca bhaviṣyasi
english: 'No sin shall be yours this day, and you shall be unconquerable; death shall have no power over you, and you shall be full of glory.'"

sanskrit: āha māṃ bhagavān evaṃ śikhaṇḍī śivavigrahaḥ yad avāptaṃ ca me sarvaṃ prasādāt tasya dhīmataḥ
english: "Thus the Blessed One, the crested one whose very form is Śiva, spoke to me; and all that I have attained is by the grace of that wise god."

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva prāha pāṇḍusutaṃ nṛpam śāpāc chakrasya kaunteya cito dharmo 'naśan mama tan me dharmaṃ yaśaś cāgryam āyuś caivādadad bhavaḥ
english: And Asita Devala addressed the king, the son of Pāṇḍu: "By a curse of Śakra, O son of Kuntī, my accumulated merit was perishing; but Bhava restored to me that merit, my foremost glory, and my life as well."

sanskrit: ṛṣir gṛtsamado nāma śakrasya dayitaḥ sakhā prāhājamīḍhaṃ bhagavān bṛhaspatisamadyutiḥ
english: The seer named Gṛtsamada, the beloved friend of Śakra, blessed and radiant as Bṛhaspati, addressed the descendant of Ajamīḍha:

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho nāma bhagavāṃś cākṣuṣasya manoḥ sutaḥ śatakrator acintyasya satre varṣasahasrike vartamāne 'bravīd vākyaṃ sāmni hy uccārite mayā
english: "The blessed one named Vasiṣṭha, son of Manu Cākṣuṣa, while the inconceivable Śatakratu's sacrificial session of a thousand years was in progress, spoke these words when a Sāman had been chanted by me:

sanskrit: rathantaraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha na samyag iti vartate samīkṣasva punar buddhyā harṣaṃ tyaktvā dvijottama ayajñavāhinaṃ pāpam akārṣīs tvaṃ sudurmate
english: 'O best of the twice-born, the Rathantara is not rightly rendered; consider it again with your mind, casting off your excitement, O foremost of the twice-born. You have committed a sin that bears no sacrifice, O most wicked-minded one.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahākrodhāt prāha ruṣṭaḥ punar vacaḥ prajñayā rahito duḥkhī nityaṃ bhīto vanecaraḥ daśa varṣasahasrāṇi daśāṣṭau ca śatāni ca
english: Having spoken thus, in great wrath he angrily uttered these further words: 'Bereft of wisdom, wretched, forever fearful, a wanderer of the woods shall you become—for ten thousand years and ten and eight hundred more,

sanskrit: naṣṭapānīyayavase mṛgair anyaiś ca varjite ayajñīyadrume deśe rurusiṃhaniṣevite bhavitā tvaṃ mṛgaḥ krūro mahāduḥkhasamanvitaḥ
english: in a region without water or pasture, shunned by deer and other beasts, with no trees fit for sacrifice, haunted by antelope and lion—there you shall become a savage beast beset with great suffering.'

sanskrit: tasya vākyasya nidhane pārtha jāto hy ahaṃ mṛgaḥ tato māṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptaṃ prāha yogī maheśvaraḥ
english: At the close of that utterance, O Pārtha, I was indeed born a beast; then, when I had come to him for refuge, the yogin Maheśvara said to me:

sanskrit: ajaraś cāmaraś caiva bhavitā duḥkhavarjitaḥ sāmyaṃ samas tu te saukhyaṃ yuvayor vardhatāṃ kratuḥ
english: 'Ageless and deathless shall you become, free of sorrow; even and equable shall your happiness be—and may the sacrificial rite of you both prosper.'"

sanskrit: anugrahān evam eṣa karoti bhagavān vibhuḥ paraṃ dhātā vidhātā ca sukhaduḥkhe ca sarvadā
english: "Thus does this Blessed and all-pervading Lord bestow his favors—the supreme Ordainer and Disposer, and ever the giver of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: acintya eṣa bhagavān karmaṇā manasā girā na me tāta yudhiśreṣṭha vidyayā paṇḍitaḥ samaḥ
english: Inconceivable is this Blessed One in deed, in thought, and in speech; not even one learned in knowledge, dear child, O best of warriors, is his equal."

sanskrit: jaigīṣavya uvāca mamāṣṭaguṇam aiśvaryaṃ dattaṃ bhagavatā purā yatnenālpena balinā vārāṇasyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira
english: Jaigīṣavya said: "The eightfold lordly power was given to me of old by the mighty Blessed One, with but little effort, at Vārāṇasī, O Yudhiṣṭhira."

sanskrit: gārgya uvāca catuḥṣaṣṭyaṅgam adadāt kālajñānaṃ mamādbhutam sarasvatyās taṭe tuṣṭo manoyajñena pāṇḍava
english: Gārgya said: "The wondrous knowledge of time, with its sixty-four branches, he gave to me, well pleased by a sacrifice of the mind, upon the bank of the Sarasvatī, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tulyaṃ mama sahasraṃ tu sutānāṃ brahmavādinām āyuś caiva saputrasya saṃvatsaraśatāyutam
english: And he gave me a thousand sons, all alike, expounders of the sacred word, and a lifespan—for me together with my sons—of a hundred and ten thousand years."

sanskrit: parāśara uvāca prasādyāhaṃ purā śarvaṃ manasācintayaṃ nṛpa mahātapā mahātejā mahāyogī mahāyaśāḥ vedavyāsaḥ śriyāvāso brahmaṇyaḥ karuṇātmakaḥ
english: Parāśara said: "Having propitiated Śarva of old, O king, I pondered in my mind—desiring a son of great austerity, great splendor, great yoga, and great fame, a Vedavyāsa, an abode of glory, devoted to brahman, and compassionate of nature:

sanskrit: api nāmepsitaḥ putro mama syād vai maheśvarāt iti matvā hṛdi mataṃ prāha māṃ surasattamaḥ
english: 'Might there be granted to me from Maheśvara the son I desire?' Knowing this resolve in my heart, the best of the gods spoke to me:

sanskrit: mayi saṃbhavatas tasya phalāt kṛṣṇo bhaviṣyati sāvarṇasya manoḥ sarge saptarṣiś ca bhaviṣyati
english: 'As the fruit of his being born of me, he shall be Kṛṣṇa, and in the creation of Manu Sāvarṇa he shall be one of the seven seers.

sanskrit: vedānāṃ ca sa vai vyastā kuruvaṃśakaras tathā itihāsasya kartā ca putras te jagato hitaḥ
english: He shall be the divider of the Vedas and the continuer of the Kuru line, and the author of the epic history; your son shall be a benefactor of the world.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati mahendrasya dayitaḥ sa mahāmuniḥ ajaraś cāmaraś caiva parāśara sutas tava
english: That great sage shall become beloved of Mahendra, ageless and deathless, O Parāśara—he, your son.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa bhagavāṃs tatraivāntaradhīyata yudhiṣṭhira mahāyogī vīryavān akṣayo 'vyayaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, that Blessed One vanished then and there, O Yudhiṣṭhira—the great yogin, the valiant, the imperishable, the undecaying."

sanskrit: māṇḍavya uvāca acauraś cauraśaṅkāyāṃ śūle bhinno hy ahaṃ yadā tatrasthena stuto devaḥ prāha māṃ vai maheśvaraḥ
english: Māṇḍavya said: "When, though no thief, on suspicion of theft I was impaled upon the stake, I praised the god while fixed there, and Maheśvara said to me:

sanskrit: mokṣaṃ prāpsyasi śūlāc ca jīviṣyasi samārbudam rujā śūlakṛtā caiva na te vipra bhaviṣyati ādhibhir vyādhibhiś caiva varjitas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
english: 'You shall be freed from the stake, and you shall live a hundred million years; nor shall the pain caused by the stake be yours, O brāhmaṇa, and free of mental and bodily afflictions shall you be.

sanskrit: pādāc caturthāt saṃbhūta ātmā yasmān mune tava tvaṃ bhaviṣyasy anupamo janma vai saphalaṃ kuru
english: Since your self, O sage, has come forth from the fourth quarter, you shall be without compare; make your birth bear fruit indeed.

sanskrit: tīrthābhiṣekaṃ saphalaṃ tvam avighnena cāpsyasi svargaṃ caivākṣayaṃ vipra vidadhāmi tavorjitam
english: The fruitful bathing in sacred fords you shall attain without hindrance, and an imperishable heaven, mighty and exalted, I bestow upon you, O brāhmaṇa.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu bhagavān vareṇyo vṛṣavāhanaḥ maheśvaro mahārāja kṛttivāsā mahādyutiḥ sagaṇo daivataśreṣṭhas tatraivāntaradhīyata
english: Having spoken thus, the Blessed One, the most excellent, borne upon the bull, Maheśvara, O great king, clad in his hide and of mighty radiance, foremost of the gods together with his hosts, vanished then and there."

sanskrit: gālava uvāca viśvāmitrābhyanujñāto hy ahaṃ pitaram āgataḥ abravīn māṃ tato mātā duḥkhitā rudatī bhṛśam
english: Gālava said: "Dismissed with leave by Viśvāmitra, I came to my father; then my mother, sorrowing and weeping bitterly, said to me:

sanskrit: kauśikenābhyanujñātaṃ putraṃ vedavibhūṣitam na tāta taruṇaṃ dāntaṃ pitā tvāṃ paśyate 'nagha
english: 'Your father does not behold you, dear child—his son adorned with the Vedas, dismissed with leave by Kauśika, young, self-controlled, and sinless.'

sanskrit: śrutvā jananyā vacanaṃ nirāśo gurudarśane niyatātmā mahādevam apaśyaṃ so 'bravīc ca mām
english: Hearing my mother's words, despairing of seeing my father, with self subdued I beheld Mahādeva, and he said to me:

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca te tvaṃ ca putra mṛtyuvivarjitāḥ bhaviṣyatha viśa kṣipraṃ draṣṭāsi pitaraṃ kṣaye
english: 'Your father and your mother and you yourself, my son, shall be free of death; enter quickly, and you shall behold your father in his dwelling.'

sanskrit: anujñāto bhagavatā gṛhaṃ gatvā yudhiṣṭhira apaśyaṃ pitaraṃ tāta iṣṭiṃ kṛtvā viniḥsṛtam
english: Dismissed with leave by the Blessed One, having gone home, O Yudhiṣṭhira, I beheld my father, dear lord, just come forth from completing his offering.

sanskrit: upaspṛśya gṛhītvedhmaṃ kuśāṃś ca śaraṇād gurūn tān visṛjya ca māṃ prāha pitā sāsrāvilekṣaṇaḥ
english: Having touched water and taken up the fuel-sticks and the kuśa grass, and having set down those holy implements within the dwelling, my father, his eyes brimming with tears, said to me—

sanskrit: praṇamantaṃ pariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya pāṇḍava diṣṭyā dṛṣṭo 'si me putra kṛtavidya ihāgataḥ
english: embracing me as I bowed and smelling my head, O Pāṇḍava: 'By good fortune are you seen by me, my son, accomplished in learning and come here at last.'"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāny atyadbhutāny eva karmāṇy atha mahātmanaḥ proktāni munibhiḥ śrutvā vismayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard these most wondrous deeds of the great-souled one recounted by the sages, the Pāṇḍava was filled with amazement.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo 'bravīd vākyaṃ punar matimatāṃ varaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dharmanityaṃ puruhūtam iveśvaraḥ
english: Then Kṛṣṇa, foremost of the wise, spoke again to Yudhiṣṭhira, ever devoted to dharma, as the Lord might speak to Indra of the many invocations:

sanskrit: ādityacandrāv anilānalau ca; dyaur bhūmir āpo vasavo 'tha viśve dhātāryamā śukrabṛhaspatī ca; rudrāḥ sasādhyā varuṇo vittagopaḥ
english: "The sun and moon, the wind and fire, the sky, the earth, the waters, the Vasus, the All-gods, the Ordainer, Aryaman, Śukra and Bṛhaspati, the Rudras together with the Sādhyas, Varuṇa the guardian of wealth,

sanskrit: brahmā śakro māruto brahma satyaṃ; vedā yajñā dakṣiṇā vedavāhāḥ somo yaṣṭā yac ca havyaṃ haviś ca; rakṣā dīkṣā niyamā ye ca ke cit
english: Brahmā, Śakra, the Wind, the sacred word, truth, the Vedas, the sacrifices, the priestly fee, the bearers of the Vedas, Soma, the sacrificer, and whatever is offered and the oblation itself, protection, consecration, and whatever observances there are,

sanskrit: svāhā vaṣaḍ brāhmaṇāḥ saurabheyā; dharmaṃ cakraṃ kālacakraṃ caraṃ ca yaśo damo buddhimatī sthitiś ca; śubhāśubhaṃ munayaś caiva sapta
english: the cries Svāhā and Vaṣaṭ, the brāhmaṇas, the offspring of the divine cow, dharma, the wheel and the moving wheel of time, glory, self-restraint, intelligent steadfastness, the auspicious and the inauspicious, and the seven sages—

sanskrit: agryā buddhir manasā darśane ca; sparśe siddhiḥ karmaṇāṃ yā ca siddhiḥ gaṇā devānām ūṣmapāḥ somapāś ca; lekhāḥ suyāmās tuṣitā brahmakāyāḥ
english: the foremost intellect, perception by mind and sight, attainment in touch, and the attainment that crowns deeds, the hosts of the gods—the drinkers of warm vapor and the drinkers of Soma, the Lekhas, the Suyāmas, the Tuṣitas, the Brahmakāyas,

sanskrit: ābhāsvarā gandhapā dṛṣṭipāś ca; vācā viruddhāś ca manoviruddhāḥ śuddhāś ca nirvāṇaratāś ca devāḥ; sparśāśanā darśapā ājyapāś ca
english: the Ābhāsvaras, the drinkers of fragrance, the sustainers of sight, those opposed in speech and those opposed in mind, the pure gods and those who delight in extinction, those who feed on touch, the beholders, and the drinkers of clarified butter—

sanskrit: cintāgatā ye ca deveṣu mukhyā; ye cāpy anye devatāś cājamīḍha suparṇagandharvapiśācadānavā; yakṣās tathā pannagāś cāraṇāś ca
english: those who abide in thought and are chief among the gods, and whatever other deities there are, O descendant of Ajamīḍha, the Suparṇas, Gandharvas, Piśācas, and Dānavas, the Yakṣas, the serpents, and the Cāraṇas—

sanskrit: sūkṣmaṃ sthūlaṃ mṛdu yac cāpy asūkṣmaṃ; sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhaduḥkhāntaraṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ yogaṃ yat parāṇāṃ paraṃ ca; śarvāj jātaṃ viddhi yat kīrtitaṃ me
english: the subtle, the gross, the soft, and what is not subtle, pleasure, pain, and what lies between pleasure and pain, Sāṃkhya and Yoga, and what is highest of the high—know all that I have named to be sprung from Śarva.

sanskrit: tatsaṃbhūtā bhūtakṛto vareṇyāḥ; sarve devā bhuvanasyāsya gopāḥ āviśyemāṃ dharaṇīṃ ye 'bhyarakṣan; purātanīṃ tasya devasya sṛṣṭim
english: Sprung from him are the makers of beings, the most excellent; all the gods are guardians of this world, who, entering this earth, have protected the ancient creation of that god.

sanskrit: vicinvantaṃ manasā toṣṭuvīmi; kiṃ cit tattvaṃ prāṇahetor nato 'smi dadātu devaḥ sa varān iheṣṭān; abhiṣṭuto naḥ prabhur avyayaḥ sadā
english: Searching with my mind, I would praise some truth for the sake of life; I am bowed down. May that god grant the boons desired here; may the undecaying Lord, ever praised by us, bestow them."

sanskrit: imaṃ stavaṃ saṃniyamyendriyāṇi; śucir bhūtvā yaḥ puruṣaḥ paṭheta abhagnayogo niyato 'bdam ekaṃ; sa prāpnuyād aśvamedhe phalaṃ yat
english: That man who, restraining his senses and having become pure, recites this hymn with unbroken discipline, self-controlled, for one year—he would obtain the fruit that lies in the horse sacrifice.

sanskrit: vedān kṛtsnān brāhmaṇaḥ prāpnuyāc ca; jayed rājā pṛthivīṃ cāpi kṛtsnām vaiśyo lābhaṃ prāpnuyān naipuṇaṃ ca; śūdro gatiṃ pretya tathā sukhaṃ ca
english: A brāhmaṇa would gain all the Vedas, a king would conquer the whole earth, a vaiśya would gain profit and skill, and a śūdra would win a good course after death and happiness as well.

sanskrit: stavarājam imaṃ kṛtvā rudrāya dadhire manaḥ sarvadoṣāpahaṃ puṇyaṃ pavitraṃ ca yaśasvinam
english: Having made this king of hymns, they fixed their minds upon Rudra—the hymn that removes all faults, meritorious, purifying, and glory-bestowing.

sanskrit: yāvanty asya śarīreṣu romakūpāṇi bhārata tāvad varṣasahasrāṇi svarge vasati mānavaḥ
english: As many as are the pores of the hair upon his body, O Bhārata, for so many thousands of years does that man dwell in heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ sahadharmeti procyate bharatarṣabha pāṇigrahaṇakāle tu strīṇām etat kathaṃ smṛtam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "This thing that is called 'shared dharma,' O bull of the Bharatas—how has it come to be enjoined for women at the time of the taking of the hand in marriage?

sanskrit: ārṣa eṣa bhaved dharmaḥ prājāpatyo 'tha vāsuraḥ yad etat sahadharmeti pūrvam uktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ
english: Is this the law of the seers, or of Prajāpati, or indeed of the asuras—this 'shared dharma' that was declared of old by the great sages?

sanskrit: saṃdehaḥ sumahān eṣa viruddha iti me matiḥ iha yaḥ sahadharmo vai pretyāyaṃ vihitaḥ kva nu
english: A very great doubt is this, and a contradiction, in my view: the shared dharma that holds here in this life—where, then, is it ordained to hold in the world beyond?

sanskrit: svarge mṛtānāṃ bhavati sahadharmaḥ pitāmaha pūrvam ekas tu mriyate kva caikas tiṣṭhate vada
english: Does shared dharma belong to the dead in heaven, O grandsire? Yet one dies first while the other remains—tell me, where then is it?"

sanskrit: nānākarmaphalopetā nānākarmanivāsinaḥ nānānirayaniṣṭhāntā mānuṣā bahavo yadā
english: "When men are many, endowed with the fruits of diverse deeds, dwelling in diverse states of action, ending in diverse hells,

sanskrit: anṛtāḥ striya ity evaṃ sūtrakāro vyavasyati yadānṛtāḥ striyas tāta sahadharmaḥ kutaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: and when the author of the aphorisms lays down that 'women are untruthful'—since women are untruthful, dear lord, whence is shared dharma enjoined for them?

sanskrit: anṛtāḥ striya ity evaṃ vedeṣv api hi paṭhyate dharmo 'yaṃ paurvikī saṃjñā upacāraḥ kriyāvidhiḥ
english: 'Women are untruthful'—even in the Vedas this is so recited. This dharma, this ancient designation, this customary usage, this rule of rites—

sanskrit: gahvaraṃ pratibhāty etan mama cintayato 'niśam niḥsaṃdeham idaṃ sarvaṃ pitāmaha yathā śrutiḥ
english: all this appears to me an impenetrable thicket as I ponder it day and night; make all of this free of doubt for me, O grandsire, as the sacred revelation has it."
